proof_summary: Since a product unequal to one cannot be indexed by the empty set, an associated prime exists (and the finite set has a maximum). For any such prime \(p\), if \(2n-p\) were composite, its least prime factor would be at most \(\sqrt{2n-p}\le\sqrt{2n}\) and would force \(p\equiv 2n\pmod q\), contradicting the defining exclusion; hence \(p\) and \(2n-p\) form a Goldbach partition, in particular when \(p\) is the maximum.
